The Fool.image: A traveler nears a cliff with a white dog at their feet; a small bundle hangs from a staff beneath a bright sun.
The Fool.general: The Fool invites a new start without demanding a complete map. Curiosity helps, while a glance at the edge keeps the step intentional.
The Fool.love: In relationships, openness can make room for someone new; keep your boundaries as you explore.
The Fool.work: Try a first draft or a small experiment before committing to the full plan.
The Fool.money: Leave room for discovery, but check the cost of a new commitment before you leap.
The Fool.reflection: What first step feels exciting and still respects your limits?

The Magician.image: One hand points upward and the other downward; a wand, cup, sword, and pentacle rest on the table among flowers.
The Magician.general: The Magician turns intention into action by noticing the tools already available. Focus makes possibilities more concrete.
The Magician.love: Say what you mean and notice whether actions match promises.
The Magician.work: Use a skill you already have to move one idea into practice.
The Magician.money: List available resources before buying another tool or taking on a new expense.
The Magician.reflection: What can you make with what is already in your hands?

The High Priestess.image: A seated figure rests between black and white pillars; a patterned veil and a scroll sit nearby.
The High Priestess.general: The High Priestess suggests listening before explaining. Some information becomes clearer through observation and time.
The High Priestess.love: Allow space for feelings that are not ready to be named; avoid assuming silence has one meaning.
The High Priestess.work: Research quietly and give an uncertain question time before presenting a conclusion.
The High Priestess.money: Pause a decision if key figures or terms remain unclear.
The High Priestess.reflection: What do you notice when you stop pressing for an immediate answer?

The Empress.image: A crowned figure sits on cushions beside wheat; trees and flowing water surround her.
The Empress.general: The Empress links growth with care, comfort, and sustained attention. What is tended has room to develop.
The Empress.love: Offer warmth and receive it too; care works best when it is mutual.
The Empress.work: Create conditions in which a project or person can grow, rather than pushing for instant results.
The Empress.money: Support what matters while keeping generosity within a workable budget.
The Empress.reflection: What in your life would benefit from regular care?

The Emperor.image: An armored ruler sits on a stone throne carved with rams; bare mountains rise behind him.
The Emperor.general: The Emperor asks where a clear framework could provide stability. Authority is most useful when paired with accountability.
The Emperor.love: Set expectations openly and make space for both people's needs.
The Emperor.work: Define ownership, deadlines, and decisions so good work has a dependable structure.
The Emperor.money: Make a plan and revisit its assumptions instead of treating a budget as a commandment.
The Emperor.reflection: Where would a firmer boundary bring relief?

The Hierophant.image: A robed teacher raises a hand between two pillars; two followers kneel before him with crossed keys below.
The Hierophant.general: The Hierophant points to shared knowledge and the communities that pass it on. Learn the rules, then decide which remain useful.
The Hierophant.love: Talk about values and expectations you may have inherited from family or culture.
The Hierophant.work: Seek mentorship, understand a process, and question it respectfully where needed.
The Hierophant.money: Read the established terms and ask for guidance before signing up to a complex arrangement.
The Hierophant.reflection: Which tradition supports you, and which one deserves review?

The Lovers.image: Two figures stand beneath an angel; a fruit tree and a flame-bearing tree frame the landscape.
The Lovers.general: The Lovers concerns an honest choice guided by values as much as attraction. Connection deepens when people choose with awareness.
The Lovers.love: Discuss what each person wants rather than relying on chemistry alone.
The Lovers.work: Choose a direction that fits your values, even when several options look appealing.
The Lovers.money: Let shared priorities guide a financial choice, especially when another person is involved.
The Lovers.reflection: What value do you want this choice to express?

The Chariot.image: An armored driver stands in a chariot before a city; black and white sphinxes face forward below.
The Chariot.general: The Chariot is forward motion shaped by self-direction. Different impulses need not agree before you can set a course.
The Chariot.love: Name a shared goal while allowing different feelings about the pace.
The Chariot.work: Focus your energy on the next milestone and keep distractions from steering the work.
The Chariot.money: Set a target and track progress without confusing speed with security.
The Chariot.reflection: What will help you stay on course without forcing everything?

Strength.image: A woman gently holds a lion's jaws; flowers and an infinity sign soften the scene.
Strength.general: Strength portrays courage as calm attention rather than domination. Patience can change a difficult interaction.
Strength.love: Meet tension with honesty and care, while preserving your boundaries.
Strength.work: Handle a challenge steadily; influence may work better than pressure.
Strength.money: Face an uncomfortable number without shame and make one manageable change.
Strength.reflection: Where can you choose steadiness over force?

The Hermit.image: A cloaked figure stands on a peak with a lantern and staff; the surrounding ground is sparse.
The Hermit.general: The Hermit makes space to hear your own thinking. A pause can guide a decision more clearly than constant input.
The Hermit.love: Ask for breathing room without disappearing from an important conversation.
The Hermit.work: Step back to review the purpose of a task before adding more activity.
The Hermit.money: Review spending privately and carefully before seeking outside opinions.
The Hermit.reflection: What becomes clearer when you give yourself quiet time?

Wheel of Fortune.image: A wheel turns in the sky with figures around its rim; winged figures occupy the four corners.
Wheel of Fortune.general: The Wheel of Fortune reminds us that conditions change. You cannot control every turn, but you can choose a response.
Wheel of Fortune.love: Be flexible when circumstances alter plans; avoid reading every shift as a verdict on the bond.
Wheel of Fortune.work: Prepare for changing priorities and adapt a plan when new information arrives.
Wheel of Fortune.money: Keep a buffer for uncertainty rather than assuming a favorable period lasts forever.
Wheel of Fortune.reflection: What is changing, and what remains within your influence?

Justice.image: A seated figure holds scales in one hand and a raised sword in the other between red curtains.
Justice.general: Justice calls for a clear-eyed look at facts, consequences, and fairness. A balanced decision may still be difficult.
Justice.love: Listen to both sides and own your part in a disagreement.
Justice.work: Check evidence and criteria before evaluating someone or making a decision.
Justice.money: Compare terms carefully and correct an imbalance you can document.
Justice.reflection: What information would make this decision fairer?

The Hanged Man.image: A calm figure hangs by one foot from a wooden frame; light surrounds the head while the other leg bends.
The Hanged Man.general: The Hanged Man suggests a chosen pause can reveal a different angle. Waiting is useful when it changes how you see.
The Hanged Man.love: Give a difficult exchange space before trying to win it.
The Hanged Man.work: Reframe a stalled problem instead of repeating the same approach.
The Hanged Man.money: Delay an optional purchase while you reconsider what you actually need.
The Hanged Man.reflection: What could you understand by looking from the opposite side?

Death.image: An armored rider carries a dark banner; figures stand nearby and a sunrise appears between distant towers.
Death.general: Death symbolizes a necessary transition rather than a literal event. Naming what has ended makes room for a new phase.
Death.love: Let a pattern end even if the relationship continues in a new form.
Death.work: Retire a method that no longer serves the work and plan the handover.
Death.money: Close an unhelpful expense or obligation before adding another.
Death.reflection: What are you ready to release with care?

Temperance.image: An angel pours liquid between two cups with one foot on land and one in water; a path leads toward the hills.
Temperance.general: Temperance is the art of adjusting proportions. A workable blend often matters more than an extreme answer.
Temperance.love: Find a pace that honors both people's needs rather than rushing agreement.
Temperance.work: Combine methods, test small changes, and leave time for learning.
Temperance.money: Balance present needs with longer-term goals through repeatable habits.
Temperance.reflection: What two things could work better together?

The Devil.image: Two figures stand with loose chains before a horned figure; a dark pedestal and torch anchor the scene.
The Devil.general: The Devil invites you to notice a habit or attachment that narrows your sense of choice. Awareness is a first step toward agency.
The Devil.love: Name patterns of control or dependence without blaming yourself for having them.
The Devil.work: Question incentives that keep you stuck in work that no longer fits.
The Devil.money: Identify the emotional pull behind a recurring expense and consider alternatives.
The Devil.reflection: Where do you have more choice than it first seems?

The Tower.image: Lightning strikes a tall tower and its crown falls; two figures tumble through a dark sky.
The Tower.general: The Tower shows a sudden break in a structure that seemed secure. The work afterward is to respond to what is real.
The Tower.love: A hard truth may change the shape of a connection; prioritize safety and honest repair.
The Tower.work: When a plan fails, stabilize the essentials before designing a replacement.
The Tower.money: Check immediate obligations and seek support before making large reactive decisions.
The Tower.reflection: What foundation needs attention after the shock?

The Star.image: A kneeling figure pours water onto land and into a pool; one large star shines above smaller stars.
The Star.general: The Star offers a quiet kind of hope after difficulty. Restoration can begin with simple, repeated care.
The Star.love: Rebuild trust through small, consistent acts rather than grand promises.
The Star.work: Reconnect with the purpose of your work and allow a gradual return of energy.
The Star.money: Make a realistic recovery plan rather than expecting one dramatic fix.
The Star.reflection: What helps you feel restored and connected to possibility?

The Moon.image: A winding path passes between two towers; a dog and wolf face the moon while a creature rises from water.
The Moon.general: The Moon speaks to ambiguity, emotion, and incomplete information. Notice the feeling without treating it as proof.
The Moon.love: Ask a question directly rather than building a story from mixed signals.
The Moon.work: Verify assumptions before acting on a vague concern or rumor.
The Moon.money: Avoid a commitment when key details remain obscured.
The Moon.reflection: Which fear or intuition needs a closer, kinder look?

The Sun.image: A child rides a white horse beneath a bright sun; sunflowers grow behind a wall.
The Sun.general: The Sun brings things into the open and invites uncomplicated recognition of what is working.
The Sun.love: Enjoy a warm moment together and speak appreciation plainly.
The Sun.work: Share a clear result and acknowledge the people who helped create it.
The Sun.money: Notice progress while keeping the practical details in view.
The Sun.reflection: What can you celebrate without minimizing the effort behind it?

Judgement.image: An angel sounds a trumpet above figures rising from open coffins; mountains stretch across the horizon.
Judgement.general: Judgement invites an honest review of the past and a response to what now calls for change.
Judgement.love: Discuss what has been learned rather than replaying old blame.
Judgement.work: Use feedback to decide what to continue, revise, or leave behind.
Judgement.money: Review past choices and set a more conscious direction from here.
Judgement.reflection: What would you choose differently with what you know now?

The World.image: A dancing figure stands inside an oval wreath; four figures appear at the corners of the card.
The World.general: The World recognizes a cycle brought to completion. The end is a chance to integrate the journey before beginning another.
The World.love: Acknowledge how a bond has grown and what the next chapter may ask of you.
The World.work: Close the project well, share the learning, and mark the achievement.
The World.money: Review what a completed goal cost and made possible before setting the next one.
The World.reflection: What deserves recognition before you move on?

Ace of Wands.image: A hand extends from a cloud holding a leafy wand; a distant castle sits beneath the hills.
Ace of Wands.general: The Ace of Wands is the first spark of a creative or energetic path. Give it a small, practical place to grow.
Ace of Wands.love: Notice a fresh attraction or a new way to bring energy to an existing bond.
Ace of Wands.work: Start the idea while motivation is present, even if the first version is rough.
Ace of Wands.money: Explore the cost of a new venture before investing beyond a test.
Ace of Wands.reflection: What small action could give this spark a real beginning?

Two of Wands.image: A figure holds a globe on a battlement; one wand is held while another is fixed to the wall.
Two of Wands.general: The Two of Wands asks you to look beyond what is familiar and choose a direction. Planning turns desire into a route.
Two of Wands.love: Talk about future plans without assuming both people want the same horizon.
Two of Wands.work: Compare two paths and decide what evidence you need before committing.
Two of Wands.money: Budget for exploration while protecting what already provides stability.
Two of Wands.reflection: Which direction is worth preparing for now?

Three of Wands.image: A figure watches ships from a high shore; three wands stand planted in the ground.
Three of Wands.general: The Three of Wands is the wait after an intentional launch. Progress may be happening beyond your immediate view.
Three of Wands.love: Allow a connection room to develop while keeping communication open.
Three of Wands.work: Follow up on work already sent out and prepare for the next phase.
Three of Wands.money: Track the return on an investment of time or money without demanding instant results.
Three of Wands.reflection: What has begun moving because of an earlier choice?

Four of Wands.image: A garland hangs between four upright wands; figures celebrate near a building in the distance.
Four of Wands.general: The Four of Wands invites you to pause at a shared milestone and feel the support around it.
Four of Wands.love: Celebrate a moment of ease or make a welcoming space together.
Four of Wands.work: Mark a completed stage before the team rushes into the next one.
Four of Wands.money: Enjoy an achievement within a budget that lets the feeling last.
Four of Wands.reflection: What milestone deserves a moment of celebration?

Five of Wands.image: Five young figures raise crossing wands in an open landscape; their movements pull in different directions.
Five of Wands.general: The Five of Wands shows energy without coordination. Conflict can become useful when the purpose is clarified.
Five of Wands.love: Separate playful difference from a disagreement that needs a real conversation.
Five of Wands.work: Give competing ideas a fair test and agree on a way to decide.
Five of Wands.money: Avoid spending simply to keep up with others.
Five of Wands.reflection: What shared rule would turn friction into progress?

Six of Wands.image: A rider wears a laurel wreath on a white horse; a crowd lifts wands around them.
Six of Wands.general: The Six of Wands recognizes a visible win and the people who helped make it possible.
Six of Wands.love: Offer sincere appreciation rather than assuming someone knows they matter.
Six of Wands.work: Share results and credit the team, then consider the next responsibility.
Six of Wands.money: Enjoy progress without treating one win as a permanent financial trend.
Six of Wands.reflection: Whose support belongs in this story of success?

Seven of Wands.image: A figure stands on higher ground with one wand; six more rise toward them from below.
Seven of Wands.general: The Seven of Wands asks what is worth defending when pressure gathers. A boundary can protect meaningful work.
Seven of Wands.love: Hold to a need without turning every disagreement into a contest.
Seven of Wands.work: Explain the reasoning behind a choice and stay open to useful feedback.
Seven of Wands.money: Protect a financial priority when competing demands appear.
Seven of Wands.reflection: What is worth standing up for, and where can you soften?

Eight of Wands.image: Eight wands fly diagonally across a clear sky above a river and green ground.
Eight of Wands.general: The Eight of Wands suggests movement after a slower period. Speed helps when direction is already clear.
Eight of Wands.love: A conversation may move quickly; check that you both understand what is being said.
Eight of Wands.work: Respond to timely opportunities, but confirm the details before sending.
Eight of Wands.money: Move on a clear task promptly without making a rushed financial commitment.
Eight of Wands.reflection: What needs a timely response, and what still needs checking?

Nine of Wands.image: A bandaged figure grips a wand; eight upright wands form a line behind them.
Nine of Wands.general: The Nine of Wands shows persistence shaped by past effort. Protection matters, but constant vigilance can be tiring.
Nine of Wands.love: Share why you feel guarded and distinguish the present from an old hurt.
Nine of Wands.work: Preserve energy near the end of a demanding task and ask for support.
Nine of Wands.money: Keep a buffer and review risk without expecting every setback to repeat.
Nine of Wands.reflection: What boundary supports you without closing you off?

Ten of Wands.image: A figure carries a heavy bundle of ten wands toward buildings in the distance; the load blocks their view.
Ten of Wands.general: The Ten of Wands asks whether responsibility has become too heavy to carry well. Rebalance before the load defines the whole journey.
Ten of Wands.love: Talk openly about an uneven share of emotional or practical labor.
Ten of Wands.work: Delegate, simplify, or renegotiate a scope that has grown beyond capacity.
Ten of Wands.money: List obligations and choose which can be reduced or postponed.
Ten of Wands.reflection: Which task could you put down or share?

Page of Wands.image: A young figure studies a sprouting wand in a dry landscape; distant pyramids rise behind them.
Page of Wands.general: The Page of Wands brings a beginner's excitement to an unfamiliar path. Ask questions and test what interests you.
Page of Wands.love: Approach a new connection with curiosity instead of a fixed script.
Page of Wands.work: Try a small creative experiment and learn from the response.
Page of Wands.money: Keep an exploratory budget modest while you discover what fits.
Page of Wands.reflection: What would you try if learning were the goal?

Knight of Wands.image: An armored rider urges a horse forward with a raised wand; the ground and pyramids suggest heat and distance.
Knight of Wands.general: The Knight of Wands acts with bold energy. Momentum is useful when paired with care for the people and details in its path.
Knight of Wands.love: Enjoy spontaneity while being clear about availability and intentions.
Knight of Wands.work: Lead a fast-moving task, then check where speed is creating rework.
Knight of Wands.money: Separate an exciting opportunity from an impulsive expense.
Knight of Wands.reflection: Where would your energy help most if you paced it?

Queen of Wands.image: A queen sits with a sunflower and wand; a black cat rests at her feet before a throne with lion motifs.
Queen of Wands.general: The Queen of Wands combines self-possession with welcome. Her presence can encourage others without shrinking herself.
Queen of Wands.love: Bring your full personality to a bond and make space for the other person too.
Queen of Wands.work: Lead with confidence, generosity, and clear ownership.
Queen of Wands.money: Spend in line with your values rather than to prove your worth.
Queen of Wands.reflection: Where can you be both visible and generous?

King of Wands.image: A crowned king holds a wand on a throne decorated with lions and salamanders; the landscape is warm and dry.
King of Wands.general: The King of Wands looks beyond the immediate task and helps others move toward a vision. Leadership still needs follow-through.
King of Wands.love: Share plans as an invitation, not a decree.
King of Wands.work: Set direction, delegate meaningfully, and remain accountable for outcomes.
King of Wands.money: Fund a long-term ambition with a plan that respects present limits.
King of Wands.reflection: How can you turn vision into responsible action?

Ace of Cups.image: A hand holds an overflowing cup from a cloud; a dove descends and streams fall into water lilies.
Ace of Cups.general: The Ace of Cups marks an opening in emotional life. You can welcome a feeling without deciding its entire future.
Ace of Cups.love: Make room for an honest conversation or a gentle beginning.
Ace of Cups.work: Reconnect with work that matters to you and notice what restores motivation.
Ace of Cups.money: Let generosity be intentional rather than an automatic obligation.
Ace of Cups.reflection: What feeling would you like to make room for?

Two of Cups.image: Two people offer cups to one another; a winged lion and intertwined staff appear above them.
Two of Cups.general: The Two of Cups centers on reciprocal attention. Agreement grows when each person can bring something of their own.
Two of Cups.love: Ask what mutual care looks like in practice, beyond a romantic ideal.
Two of Cups.work: Build a partnership with clear expectations and equal respect.
Two of Cups.money: Discuss shared spending openly before making assumptions.
Two of Cups.reflection: Where are you giving and receiving in balance?

Three of Cups.image: Three figures lift cups together while dancing; fruit and flowers lie at their feet.
Three of Cups.general: The Three of Cups celebrates the support and joy found in community. Connection is worth tending outside of major milestones.
Three of Cups.love: Make time for friends and the relationships that replenish you.
Three of Cups.work: Share credit, learn with peers, and celebrate a team result.
Three of Cups.money: Plan a social occasion that feels joyful without strain.
Three of Cups.reflection: Who would you like to celebrate with?

Four of Cups.image: A seated figure crosses their arms beneath a tree; three cups sit nearby while a hand offers another from a cloud.
Four of Cups.general: The Four of Cups points to a moment of emotional distance. Pause to understand the need beneath it before accepting or rejecting an offer.
Four of Cups.love: Name what feels missing without dismissing the care already present.
Four of Cups.work: Reassess a role or opportunity that no longer engages you.
Four of Cups.money: Avoid an automatic purchase offered as a cure for boredom.
Four of Cups.reflection: What are you overlooking while focused on what is absent?

Five of Cups.image: A cloaked figure faces three spilled cups; two remain upright behind them beside a bridge and river.
Five of Cups.general: The Five of Cups honors disappointment while showing that not everything has been lost. Recovery need not be rushed.
Five of Cups.love: Give hurt its space, then notice what support or connection remains.
Five of Cups.work: Learn from a setback without defining your ability by one outcome.
Five of Cups.money: Address a loss directly and take stock of resources still available.
Five of Cups.reflection: What remains within reach alongside the loss?

Six of Cups.image: In a village courtyard, one child offers another a flower-filled cup; more cups and buildings frame the scene.
Six of Cups.general: The Six of Cups links memory with tenderness. Revisiting the past can comfort you, provided you see the present clearly.
Six of Cups.love: Reconnect with warmth, but meet the person as they are now.
Six of Cups.work: Return to a skill or interest you once enjoyed and see what it offers today.
Six of Cups.money: Compare nostalgia for an old purchase with its usefulness now.
Six of Cups.reflection: Which memory offers guidance without holding you back?

Seven of Cups.image: A shadowed figure faces seven cups in clouds; the cups hold varied figures, treasures, and a wreath.
Seven of Cups.general: The Seven of Cups shows possibility mixed with illusion. Imagination opens doors, while clear criteria help you choose one.
Seven of Cups.love: Notice the difference between a real person and an idealized story.
Seven of Cups.work: Narrow attractive ideas to a few testable options.
Seven of Cups.money: Read the actual terms behind an appealing offer.
Seven of Cups.reflection: Which option still matters after the fantasy fades?

Eight of Cups.image: A figure walks away from stacked cups toward mountains; a moon hangs over the water and path.
Eight of Cups.general: The Eight of Cups suggests leaving something that no longer feels sufficient, even when it once mattered. The search is deliberate.
Eight of Cups.love: Consider whether a pattern can change or whether you need a different path.
Eight of Cups.work: Move toward more meaningful work with a plan for the transition.
Eight of Cups.money: Prepare the practical costs of leaving before you take the step.
Eight of Cups.reflection: What are you seeking beyond what already looks complete?

Nine of Cups.image: A seated figure folds their arms before a curved display of nine cups; the scene feels like a personal celebration.
Nine of Cups.general: The Nine of Cups invites you to enjoy a wish fulfilled and notice what made it possible. Satisfaction need not be defended.
Nine of Cups.love: Share happiness without asking a partner to supply all of it.
Nine of Cups.work: Recognize a result you worked for before moving the goalpost.
Nine of Cups.money: Enjoy a well-chosen reward while keeping future needs in view.
Nine of Cups.reflection: What is already enough to appreciate today?

Ten of Cups.image: A family lifts their arms beneath a rainbow of ten cups; children play near a home and river.
Ten of Cups.general: The Ten of Cups pictures shared happiness and a sense of home. It is an invitation to cultivate belonging, not a promise of perfection.
Ten of Cups.love: Define together what a supportive home or relationship feels like.
Ten of Cups.work: Notice how a healthy team culture supports good work.
Ten of Cups.money: Make shared financial plans that reflect everyone's needs.
Ten of Cups.reflection: What does belonging look like in your real life?

Page of Cups.image: A young figure holds a cup with a fish peeking out; waves and a bright tunic animate the scene.
Page of Cups.general: The Page of Cups encourages a curious response to an unexpected feeling or idea. Wonder can be informative without being a verdict.
Page of Cups.love: Express a feeling simply and stay open to a surprising response.
Page of Cups.work: Make room for a playful idea before judging whether it is useful.
Page of Cups.money: Pause before spending on a charming novelty; enjoy curiosity first.
Page of Cups.reflection: What would you learn by meeting surprise with openness?

Knight of Cups.image: An armored rider carries a cup on a slow-moving horse beside water; distant hills frame the route.
Knight of Cups.general: The Knight of Cups follows an ideal or heartfelt invitation. Sincerity becomes stronger when it is matched with follow-through.
Knight of Cups.love: Offer a genuine gesture and be clear about what you can sustain.
Knight of Cups.work: Pitch a creative idea with both feeling and practical steps.
Knight of Cups.money: Check whether a beautiful promise has workable terms.
Knight of Cups.reflection: How can you turn a heartfelt intention into a real act?

Queen of Cups.image: A queen sits beside the sea holding an ornate closed cup; cherubs decorate the throne and pebbles line the shore.
Queen of Cups.general: The Queen of Cups listens deeply without losing her own center. Empathy needs boundaries to remain generous.
Queen of Cups.love: Listen with care while allowing your needs to be heard too.
Queen of Cups.work: Use emotional insight to understand a team's concerns before responding.
Queen of Cups.money: Notice when spending is an attempt to soothe a feeling that needs another form of care.
Queen of Cups.reflection: What feeling deserves a compassionate boundary?

King of Cups.image: A crowned figure sits on a stone throne amid waves, holding a cup and scepter; a fish and ship appear nearby.
King of Cups.general: The King of Cups stays steady while emotions move around him. Wise care does not require suppressing what is felt.
King of Cups.love: Speak calmly about a difficult emotion rather than withdrawing from it.
King of Cups.work: Lead through tension with empathy and a clear decision.
King of Cups.money: Make choices from a settled perspective instead of a momentary mood.
King of Cups.reflection: What helps you stay open and steady at once?

Ace of Swords.image: A hand raises a sword from a cloud; a crown and wreath hang near its point above distant mountains.
Ace of Swords.general: The Ace of Swords offers a clear thought or question that cuts through confusion. Use it with care, not just force.
Ace of Swords.love: Say the honest thing with kindness and listen for the answer.
Ace of Swords.work: Define the problem precisely before reaching for a solution.
Ace of Swords.money: Get the facts and compare terms before making a choice.
Ace of Swords.reflection: What truth would make your next step clearer?

Two of Swords.image: A blindfolded figure crosses two swords beside water; rocks and a crescent moon sit behind them.
Two of Swords.general: The Two of Swords shows a decision held in suspension. Avoidance may buy time, but it cannot replace information.
Two of Swords.love: Ask what has gone unsaid rather than waiting for the tension to vanish.
Two of Swords.work: Identify the missing facts and set a date to decide.
Two of Swords.money: Compare two options on criteria you can actually verify.
Two of Swords.reflection: What information would help you uncross this decision?

Three of Swords.image: Three swords pierce a red heart; rain falls beneath heavy clouds.
Three of Swords.general: The Three of Swords acknowledges pain plainly. Naming a hurt can begin repair, even when it does not erase the feeling.
Three of Swords.love: Make room for grief or disappointment without turning it into a final story about yourself.
Three of Swords.work: Hear difficult feedback and separate the lesson from your self-worth.
Three of Swords.money: Face an unwelcome cost or loss, then plan the next practical step.
Three of Swords.reflection: What pain needs to be named before it can soften?

Four of Swords.image: A stone figure lies in a quiet chapel; three swords hang above and one rests below near stained glass.
Four of Swords.general: The Four of Swords offers a deliberate pause after strain. Rest can be part of the work, not a failure to act.
Four of Swords.love: Take a breather before resuming a difficult conversation.
Four of Swords.work: Protect time to recover and review before another demanding phase.
Four of Swords.money: Pause nonessential decisions until you can assess them calmly.
Four of Swords.reflection: What kind of rest would help you think more clearly?

Five of Swords.image: A figure gathers swords with a sharp expression; two others turn away near water under a troubled sky.
Five of Swords.general: The Five of Swords asks what a victory costs when trust is damaged. A win may need a more honest measure.
Five of Swords.love: Choose repair over scoring a point in an argument.
Five of Swords.work: Review whether competition is undermining the shared goal.
Five of Swords.money: Avoid a deal that feels like winning only because someone else loses.
Five of Swords.reflection: What would a better outcome look like for everyone involved?

Six of Swords.image: A boat carries a seated adult and child across water; a rower stands behind six upright swords.
Six of Swords.general: The Six of Swords describes movement away from difficulty toward a calmer place. The journey may still carry old concerns.
Six of Swords.love: Give a transition time rather than expecting immediate ease.
Six of Swords.work: Plan a careful handover and accept help while changing direction.
Six of Swords.money: Make a gradual financial adjustment that reduces strain.
Six of Swords.reflection: What support would make this transition gentler?

Seven of Swords.image: A figure carries five swords away from a camp while glancing back; two swords remain in the ground.
Seven of Swords.general: The Seven of Swords raises questions about strategy and what is being left unsaid. Cleverness works best with integrity.
Seven of Swords.love: Check whether privacy is healthy space or avoidance of a necessary truth.
Seven of Swords.work: Protect an idea thoughtfully, but do not let secrecy damage trust.
Seven of Swords.money: Read the fine print and be candid about risks in a shared decision.
Seven of Swords.reflection: What are you avoiding by taking the indirect route?

Eight of Swords.image: A blindfolded, loosely bound figure stands among eight swords; open ground and water remain nearby.
Eight of Swords.general: The Eight of Swords pictures feeling trapped while some movement may still be possible. A first option can be small.
Eight of Swords.love: Name a limit and ask what support could loosen it.
Eight of Swords.work: Test one assumption about a blocked task before accepting it as fixed.
Eight of Swords.money: Seek advice or a clearer view of choices when money feels constraining.
Eight of Swords.reflection: What small freedom is available from where you stand?

Nine of Swords.image: A person sits upright in bed with hands over their face; nine swords line the dark wall behind.
Nine of Swords.general: The Nine of Swords shows how worry can fill the night. The feeling is real, but it is not the whole picture.
Nine of Swords.love: Share a worry with someone safe instead of carrying it alone.
Nine of Swords.work: Write down the concern, its evidence, and one next action for daylight.
Nine of Swords.money: Separate an actual obligation from a feared scenario and seek help if needed.
Nine of Swords.reflection: Which worry needs support rather than another hour of rumination?

Ten of Swords.image: A figure lies beneath ten swords under a dark sky; light appears along the distant horizon.
Ten of Swords.general: The Ten of Swords depicts a painful endpoint, with daylight still beyond it. Stop adding weight to what is already over.
Ten of Swords.love: Let an ending be an ending and seek the care needed to recover.
Ten of Swords.work: Close a failed approach, document what happened, and protect the team from repetition.
Ten of Swords.money: Stabilize essentials before trying to recover a loss quickly.
Ten of Swords.reflection: What can you stop carrying now that this chapter has ended?

Page of Swords.image: A young figure holds a raised sword on windy ground; clouds race behind them and birds cross the sky.
Page of Swords.general: The Page of Swords brings an alert, questioning mind. Curiosity becomes useful when it is paired with listening.
Page of Swords.love: Ask directly and avoid turning uncertainty into suspicion.
Page of Swords.work: Research an idea, challenge assumptions, and share findings constructively.
Page of Swords.money: Read the details and ask basic questions before agreeing.
Page of Swords.reflection: What question would help you learn rather than defend?

Knight of Swords.image: An armored rider charges forward with a sword; the horse races through wind-bent trees and clouds.
Knight of Swords.general: The Knight of Swords acts quickly on a conviction. Speed can solve a problem or skip the people affected by it.
Knight of Swords.love: Slow an intense conversation enough to hear a response.
Knight of Swords.work: Move decisively on a clear issue while checking downstream impact.
Knight of Swords.money: Do not let urgency replace a review of risk or terms.
Knight of Swords.reflection: Where would one pause make your action more effective?

Queen of Swords.image: A queen sits with an upright sword and outstretched hand; clouds and birds cross the open sky.
Queen of Swords.general: The Queen of Swords pairs clear judgment with the experience behind it. Directness can be compassionate.
Queen of Swords.love: State a boundary plainly without making it a punishment.
Queen of Swords.work: Give specific feedback and invite a thoughtful response.
Queen of Swords.money: Use clear criteria to evaluate a decision, even if sentiment pulls elsewhere.
Queen of Swords.reflection: How can you be clear without becoming closed?

King of Swords.image: A king holds an upright sword on a carved throne; butterflies, birds, and a pale sky surround him.
King of Swords.general: The King of Swords uses reason in service of fair decisions. Authority carries a duty to explain its logic.
King of Swords.love: Make a difficult decision transparent and hear the other person's view.
King of Swords.work: Set standards consistently and review evidence before ruling.
King of Swords.money: Seek qualified advice for complex choices and document the reasoning.
King of Swords.reflection: What principle should guide this decision?

Ace of Pentacles.image: A hand offers a pentacle from a cloud above a garden; a path leads through an arch toward mountains.
Ace of Pentacles.general: The Ace of Pentacles is a tangible opening. A promising resource grows through steady care and realistic steps.
Ace of Pentacles.love: Notice the practical ways a bond could become more supportive.
Ace of Pentacles.work: Give a new skill or offer a concrete trial with a clear next step.
Ace of Pentacles.money: Examine the terms of an opportunity and plan how to use it well.
Ace of Pentacles.reflection: What small investment could support lasting growth?

Two of Pentacles.image: A figure moves two pentacles within an infinity loop; ships rise and fall on waves behind them.
Two of Pentacles.general: The Two of Pentacles is the ongoing work of balancing changing demands. Flexibility helps more than pretending all tasks weigh the same.
Two of Pentacles.love: Talk about time and energy so neither person has to guess.
Two of Pentacles.work: Reprioritize openly when two demands compete for the same hour.
Two of Pentacles.money: Track cash flow and adjust timing before taking on another commitment.
Two of Pentacles.reflection: What can shift to make this balance sustainable?

Three of Pentacles.image: A craftsperson works beneath an arch while two others look at plans; three pentacles decorate the stone above.
Three of Pentacles.general: The Three of Pentacles values skill built with others. Good work improves through clear roles and useful feedback.
Three of Pentacles.love: Treat a shared goal as something both people help build.
Three of Pentacles.work: Ask for specific feedback and recognize different expertise on the team.
Three of Pentacles.money: Price a project using real labor and materials, not guesswork.
Three of Pentacles.reflection: Whose perspective could improve the work?

Four of Pentacles.image: A seated figure holds one pentacle while another rests on their head and two lie beneath their feet; a city stands behind.
Four of Pentacles.general: The Four of Pentacles asks whether protection has become rigidity. Security matters, but so does room to move.
Four of Pentacles.love: Notice whether fear of loss is limiting generosity or trust.
Four of Pentacles.work: Preserve a core resource while allowing considered experiments.
Four of Pentacles.money: Build a buffer, then decide what level of saving supports life rather than constrains it.
Four of Pentacles.reflection: What are you holding tightly, and why?

Five of Pentacles.image: Two figures walk through snow past a bright stained-glass window bearing five pentacles.
Five of Pentacles.general: The Five of Pentacles acknowledges strain and the isolation it can create. Support may be nearer than it feels.
Five of Pentacles.love: Ask for practical care without assuming you must manage hardship alone.
Five of Pentacles.work: Tell someone what resources or accommodations would help.
Five of Pentacles.money: Seek assistance and prioritize essentials before facing a shortfall alone.
Five of Pentacles.reflection: Where might help be available if you ask?

Six of Pentacles.image: A standing figure weighs scales while offering coins to two kneeling people; six pentacles float above.
Six of Pentacles.general: The Six of Pentacles looks at how resources move between people. Fairness includes both generosity and the power around it.
Six of Pentacles.love: Discuss whether care and effort flow both ways.
Six of Pentacles.work: Share opportunities transparently and recognize unequal access to support.
Six of Pentacles.money: Give or receive help with clear expectations and respect.
Six of Pentacles.reflection: What would make this exchange more equitable?

Seven of Pentacles.image: A gardener leans on a tool beside a vine bearing pentacles; one coin rests near their feet.
Seven of Pentacles.general: The Seven of Pentacles is a pause to assess growth after sustained effort. Patience and evaluation belong together.
Seven of Pentacles.love: Notice what a relationship has grown through consistent care.
Seven of Pentacles.work: Review results and decide what to keep tending or change.
Seven of Pentacles.money: Assess the return on a long-term effort without reacting to one day.
Seven of Pentacles.reflection: What has grown, and what still needs time?

Eight of Pentacles.image: A craftsperson works at a bench on a pentacle; finished pieces line a post and a town sits in the distance.
Eight of Pentacles.general: The Eight of Pentacles honors repeated practice. Improvement comes from attention to the next piece, not instant mastery.
Eight of Pentacles.love: Show care through dependable small actions.
Eight of Pentacles.work: Build a skill through deliberate repetition and useful feedback.
Eight of Pentacles.money: Invest in training or tools when they serve a clear craft or goal.
Eight of Pentacles.reflection: What practice would make your work stronger?

Nine of Pentacles.image: A woman stands in a vineyard with a hooded falcon on her glove; pentacles and a small snail appear among the vines.
Nine of Pentacles.general: The Nine of Pentacles celebrates independence earned through patient cultivation. Enjoyment is part of the result.
Nine of Pentacles.love: Value closeness without giving up the space that helps you flourish.
Nine of Pentacles.work: Recognize the expertise and autonomy you have built.
Nine of Pentacles.money: Enjoy a well-earned comfort while maintaining the habits that support it.
Nine of Pentacles.reflection: What have you created that lets you feel at home with yourself?

Ten of Pentacles.image: An older figure sits near dogs beneath an arch while a family gathers; ten pentacles are woven across the scene.
Ten of Pentacles.general: The Ten of Pentacles considers what lasts beyond one moment: family, shared resources, and systems of support.
Ten of Pentacles.love: Talk about the kind of home or community you want to build together.
Ten of Pentacles.work: Design work that can be maintained and passed on clearly.
Ten of Pentacles.money: Plan for long-term needs and communicate across generations where relevant.
Ten of Pentacles.reflection: What do you hope to leave stronger for others?

Page of Pentacles.image: A young figure gazes at a pentacle above a green field; trees and mountains lie beyond.
Page of Pentacles.general: The Page of Pentacles approaches a practical opportunity as a learner. Careful attention is the beginning of skill.
Page of Pentacles.love: Learn what helps a connection feel reliable, one action at a time.
Page of Pentacles.work: Choose a skill to study and give it regular practice.
Page of Pentacles.money: Research a new financial idea before committing significant resources.
Page of Pentacles.reflection: What practical subject are you ready to learn?

Knight of Pentacles.image: An armored rider sits on a still dark horse holding a pentacle; plowed fields stretch behind them.
Knight of Pentacles.general: The Knight of Pentacles advances slowly and reliably. Consistency is powerful when the direction still matters.
Knight of Pentacles.love: Show care through follow-through rather than promises alone.
Knight of Pentacles.work: Maintain a steady process and check that routine serves the goal.
Knight of Pentacles.money: Use a repeatable plan and review it before changing course.
Knight of Pentacles.reflection: Where would patient consistency help most?

Queen of Pentacles.image: A queen studies a pentacle on a carved throne amid flowers and trees; a rabbit appears near the ground.
Queen of Pentacles.general: The Queen of Pentacles creates support through practical care. Comfort is built, maintained, and shared within limits.
Queen of Pentacles.love: Offer tangible support while making room for your own needs.
Queen of Pentacles.work: Create a workable environment where people can do good work.
Queen of Pentacles.money: Spend on what sustains daily life and keep care within your means.
Queen of Pentacles.reflection: What practical act of care would matter today?

King of Pentacles.image: A crowned figure holds a pentacle and scepter on a throne; vines, grapes, and a castle fill the scene.
King of Pentacles.general: The King of Pentacles treats resources as a responsibility, not only a reward. Stability grows through stewardship.
King of Pentacles.love: Build trust through dependable actions and shared planning.
King of Pentacles.work: Lead with sound systems and invest in people as well as outcomes.
King of Pentacles.money: Protect what has been built while deciding where it can do good.
King of Pentacles.reflection: How can you use your resources responsibly?
